text: The S1 table row of the Ownership Map is incomplete: valuation_ext is created and owned in rwb_valuation by RWB-S1-E4002-APP, keyed uniquely on valuation_key, with stale_flag and age_days written at receipt and accepted, accepted_at and accepted_by written by FEAT-VAL-04. The appraisal facts are never copied into rwb_valuation.
why: The context pack lists no S1 table while the legacy story and TSD S1 both give the service a valuation row with DF-EXT and DF-COL identifiers; DP-01 requires the row to live in the owning service's schema.
read: Context pack S1 ownership rows ('Tables (0)'); legacy RWB-E4-002 data row; TSD S1 T3.1 valuation fields; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-01
confirm: Solution architect, S1, with the owner of the ownership map, before the wave 3 database story is baselined
impact: If refused, the valuation row must be published by the service that owns it and this key's table is dropped; the read and the decision record are unaffected

text: The receipt of the appraisal has no clock of its own: the read and the valuation_ext write run inside the route assessment served by POST /cases/{caseId}/route, and the batch leg of the FSD trigger phrase is asserted by the freshness gate VR-S1-002-1 on recovery.v_ace_batch_status. No Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job is created for it.
why: The FSD names 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer' as the trigger, but the S1 ownership rows give the service no event and no job, and DP-10 is not among the patterns this key applies.
read: FSD S1 A2.2.2 step 1; context pack S1 ownership rows ('Events (0)', 'Jobs (0)'); FSD S1 A2.2.3.1 VR-S1-002-1
confirm: Solution architect, S1, and the owner of the ACE batch schedule
impact: If a schedule is needed later it is a DP-10 story with H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON; the read, the row and the record are unchanged

text: rwb-valuation reads recovery.v_ace_valuation, recovery.v_ace_collateral and recovery.v_ace_batch_status SELECT-only through its own login, as the second option of DP-05, and adds no REST dependency on rwb-source-data. rwb-source-data owns the views and grants the read.
why: The legacy story and FSD S1 read the views directly, DP-05 allows the service's own ACE views, and Architecture v5 states that the v_ace_* views are read only by rwb-source-data; the split adopts the direct read so that no contract dependency is created.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-002 story and data rows; FSD S1 A2.2.2 integration points; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 8 notes
confirm: Owner of rwb-source-data and the owner of the ACE view catalogue, before the wave 3 schema and grant story
impact: If the direct read is refused, the facts arrive through the rwb-source-data contract and this key gains a contract dependency of class C; the business behaviour is unchanged

text: Of the three REST operations the S1 ownership rows carry, POST /cases/{caseId}/route belongs to RWB-E4-002 because it is the operation the legacy story names; the two asset valuation operations POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations and POST /assets/{assetKey}/valuations belong to the sibling valuation keys of the service and are published by their contracts.
why: Neither the legacy story nor the FSD attributes the two asset valuation operations to this feature, and publishing them here would declare operations no acceptance criterion of this key covers.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-002 endpoints row; context pack S1 REST operations provided; FSD S1 A2.2
confirm: Solution architect, S1, against the sibling valuation work packages
impact: If wrong, one contract declares two extra operations and the sibling key loses them; no table, rule or message changes

text: Where the legacy data row and TSD S1 name the same column, the TSD type stands: valuation_ext is the row TSD S1 T3.1 calls valuation for the Workbench-owned columns (valuer_partner_id, accepted, stale_flag, age_days), the appraisal elements sit flat inside Approval, the valuation_ext column types are those of T3.1, and the 404, 409 and retention wording is carried as messageId slots and an open P3 item.
why: The contract must publish a frozen shape on Day 1, and the legacy row names 14 field identifiers with 'and 8 more' while the TSD gives types for four of them and no nesting rule, no conflict text and no retention rule.
read: TSD S1 T3.0, T3.1, T-A.2; legacy RWB-E4-002 data and validation rows
confirm: Platform API owner and solution architect, S1, at the v1 freeze
impact: A refused nesting or type is a breaking change before the first consumer pins v1; after publication it is a major version 2

text: FSD S1 v3 and TSD S1 v2 carry status 'In review' and no approval of them is recorded for this run; both are treated as a Draft baseline that the split may build against, and every output of this key is at status Draft (realignment v1).
why: The overlay for D-RCV-60 records a missing approval or status as an assumption and continues at Draft rather than stopping the run.
read: FSD S1 document control ('Status: In review'); TSD S1 document control ('Status: In review'); AGENTS.md rule 9
confirm: Business lead and solution architect, S1, at the next review point
impact: An approved version may change a field, a list or a right; the change is then a new version of the contract, not an edit of v1
